claims.quote: On November 26, 2024, an issue pertaining to incomplete software recall remedies was brought to Ford’s Critical Concern Group (CCRG) for review.

events.quote: On November 26, 2024, an issue pertaining to incomplete software recall remedies was brought to Ford’s Critical Concern Group (CCRG) for review.
This issue was initially identified in a Quality Office forum, where an audit was requested for software part numbers applied to vehicles remedied under a sample of field service actions (FSAs).
Initial review of three FSAs revealed insufficient data to confirm correct software application across all FSAs using the current field service tool, known as FDRS.
CCRG decided to conduct further investigation.
In December 2024, a cross-functional team was formed to audit all software FSAs that used the FDRS service tool, with its first focus being on safety and compliance FSAs.
Templates were created to track software lineage part numbers.

On December 19, 2024, Ford informed NHTSA of this concern -- the service tool data confirmed that the software state on the service tool at the time of installation matches the FSA software release for most vehicles.
However, there are vehicles that do not have a match between the software state on the service tool and the FSA software release.
Ford discussed with NHTSA its plan to address the mismatched vehicles.
In January 2025, the cross-functional team created database records to store all software lineage part numbers for previously launched FSAs.
The team then began auditing the current software level for every VIN repaired under several previously launched FSAs.
The audit revealed that implementation inconsistencies found in FDRS could also be present within the IDS software as well as a significant lack of historical data.
Further investigation was deemed necessary.
Results of this harvest program showed that in some FSAs, the intended remedy software may not have been successfully applied to all vehicles.
The CCRG determined that several FSAs that had a recall remedy implemented using the IDS tool may have been closed without that remedy being installed.
As a result, an activity was initiated to verify the software levels of vehicles that previously received these FSA repairs.

The VINs included in this program are both (1) VINs confirmed to Docusign Envelope ID: 145AE4F6-3424-83B1-82C7-B899A0DC17E0 contain the incorrect software, and (2) VINs with a closed FSA, but the software version cannot be confirmed due to gaps in the records.
On May 27, 2026, Ford's audit team confirmed that the software state matched the FSA software release in a subset of vehicles out of the total population of completed FSA 18S32 remedy repairs.
On June 2, 2026, Ford’s Field Review Committee reviewed the concern and approved a field action.

On June 12, 2026, following an investigation into the 18S32 workflow, Ford discovered that the population for 26S40 did not include certain affected VINs that fall outside of the US but are located in US federal territories.

In March 2025, during a comprehensive audit of software-related FSAs dating back to 2017, discrepancies were identified during the transition between the legacy field service tool, known as IDS, and the new FDRS service tool.
In November 2025, a harvest program was approved to assess the success of remedies applied using the IDS tool for programs administered during this transition period.
On April 16, 2026, the matter was presented to the Critical Concern Review Group (CCRG).
On July 7, 2026, Ford’s Field Review Committee reviewed the concern and approved an amendment to the population of the field action.

events.quote: On February 19, 2026, an issue pertaining to loss of Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System (AVAS) (also referred to as Pedestrian Alert System (PAS)) function on vehicles that had previously received the remedy for Ford’s Safety Recall 25SA2 was brought to Ford’s Critical Concern Review Group for review.

Safety Recall 25SA2 addressed the loss of PAS functionality due to a software-related defect within the Digital Signal Processor (DSP) or the Audio Control Module (ACM) of certain hybrid electric vehicles.
The remedy for 25SA2 was a software update that Ford made available through dealer service on October 29, 2025.
On February 26, 2026, CCRG requested a pause in the deployment of this service remedy due to post-recall complaints for the loss of PAS functionality.
In these complaints, many drivers reported observing a message on the Instrument Panel Cluster stating "Pedestrian Sounder Fault.
Service Now".
In March and April 2026, CCRG analyzed warranty claims and began its technical investigation.
First, CCRG binned the post-recall complaints against the different audio architectures.
In total, for the HEVs, there are three different audio systems: the base audio system, the 12-channel DSP system, and the 24- channel DSP system.
The team identified a potential software issue within the 24-channel DSP system on Nautilus HEV vehicles that can cause a loss of PAS function.

However, this causal factor accounted for a portion of the warranty claims associated with this topic and did not fully explain why there was a loss of PAS functionality after receiving the 25SA2 remedy.
CCRG continued its investigation.

In May and June 2026, CCRG identified an additional concern that appears to affect all audio systems on the Nautilus HEV and Explorer HEV vehicle variants and leads to intermittent loss of PAS function.

In May and June 2026, CCRG identified an additional concern that appears to affect all audio systems on the Nautilus HEV and Explorer HEV vehicle variants and leads to intermittent loss of PAS function.

While the precise cause of this condition remains under investigation, CCRG believes that the condition appears to be related to vehicles detecting a loss of communication between the Audio Control Module (ACM) and the Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM).
When this occurs, two specific Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) are recorded.
Based on a review of connected vehicle data and customer interviews, CCRG believes drivers may randomly lose PAS function for a key cycle.

It is not known at this time if the loss of PAS function is due to a communication loss occurring between the ACM and the APIM or if there is an error in the detection and response strategy that results in DTCs and subsequent loss of PAS function.
On June 23, 2026, Ford’s Field Review Committee reviewed the concerns and approved a field action; however, the remedy was not fully described as more root cause investigation was needed.

By late June and July 2026, Ford’s Audio and IVI teams determined that the additional PAS system concern is related to a transient interaction between the ACM and the Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) rather than a persistent hardware defect.
Analysis of CAN message history on test vehicles led to the understanding that DTCs typically occur during initialization of the audio bus at vehicle start.
Additional analysis of retail vehicle connected data found that most audio system faults take place while the vehicle is in Park.
In summary, this is a momentary condition during vehicle startup, usually while the vehicle is in Park, and results in unavailability of the PAS function for the remainder of the key cycle.
On July 21, 2026, Ford’s Field Review Committee reviewed the proposed remedy and approved an amendment to the 26S51 field action.
In March and April 2026, CCRG analyzed warranty claims and began its technical investigation.

events_excluded.sentence: As of May 1, 2026, Ford is aware of 65 warranty claims on model year 2024–2026 Nautilus HEV vehicles and 7 warranty claims on model year 2025–2026 Explorer HEV vehicles alleging post-25SA2 PAS issues.
Ford is not aware of any reports of accident or injury related to this condition.

events.quote: In April 2025, BMW became aware of an increasing number of ignition locks on S 1000 RR models replaced under warranty.
An engineering investigation was initiated.
Field parts were requested to be returned for analysis.
At that time, the rate of occurrence in the field was less than 0.1%.
Between May and November, parts were returned, and analyzed.
Preliminary information suggested that vibration-induced wear on the contact pin within the ignition lock could occur.
However, further analysis was necessary to understand specific conditions in which vibration could play a role and, if so, the specific parameters or characteristics involved with vibration.
Further investigations were initiated as a systematic pattern was not yet clear from an examination of the field cases.
Among other factors, the possible influence of decoupling of the fork bridge was analyzed using NVH profiles, and comparing these profiles with S 1000 RR model updates that had occurred since 2018.
Additional evaluations involved comparing these analyses with other, similar, four- cylinder models.
The ongoing field observation indicated that the rate of occurrence remained at less than 0.1%.
By June, the rate of occurrence in the field was less than approximately 0.5%, which indicated that, as mileage increased, the rate of occurrence could also increase.
On July 16, 2026, BMW decided to conduct a voluntary safety recall.
Between November 2025 and April 2026, the investigation continued, and was focused on analysis of the wear process of the contact pin.
In April 2026, a detailed analysis involving field data, and statistical forecasting, was initiated.

events.quote: In November 2025 Heil learned that a ladder mounting bracket may have been assembled with a bolt longer than specified in one leg of the ladder support structure on a customer unit.
The longer bolt reduced the designed clearance between the bolt and an adjacent CNG cylinder.

No evidence of contact or interference with the CNG cylinder on that customer’s unit was identified at that time; however, The Heil Co. initiated an investigation to evaluate the potential for cylinder-to-bolt contact.
Inspection identified surface blemishes on seven (7) cylinders in an area corresponding to the location of the ladder mounting bolt.
Measurements of the observed blemishes were evaluated against the cylinder manufacturer's damage assessment criteria and were determined to be within repairable limits.
The Heil Co. continued its investigation to determine the mechanism by which the observed blemishes could occur.
The investigation considered both original vehicle assembly and subsequent service activities.

The investigation determined that installation of an incorrect bolt at one particular location during vehicle assembly or during subsequent service and inspection activities could reduce the intended clearance between the ladder structure and the cylinder.
The investigation continued through July and early August 2026.

Based on the investigation findings, The Heil Co. concluded that an incorrect bolt could potentially be installed in the affected location and could reduce the designed clearance to the adjacent CNG cylinder, creating the potential for cylinder contact and damage.
To eliminate the possibility of incorrect bolt installation at this location, The Heil Co. implemented a design change on August 4, 2026, removing the ladder support leg containing the subject bolt .
On August 11, 2026, The Heil Co. determined that the condition described above constituted a safety- related defect and decided to conduct a voluntary safety recall.
With the exception of the 14 vehicles inspected as described above, there have been no other warranty claims, customer complaints, or field reports on this issue.
Between February and March 2026, The Heil Co. removed and inspected CNG cylinders from fourteen (14) customer vehicles equipped with the same ladder configuration.

From November 2025 through February 2026, MBAG identified candidate vehicles and markets, developed the collection protocol, and coordinated the retrieval and shipment of the requested components.
By June 2026, the requested brake hose components had been collected and returned to MBAG.
MBAG forwarded the components to the supplier for detailed technical analysis and testing.
In July 2026, MBAG reviewed and discussed the results of the supplier’s laboratory and durability testing for the retrieved field parts.

Based on the additional field reports, the analysis of the retrieved components, and the resulting laboratory and durability testing, MBAG reassessed the affected vehicle population with respect to production range and climatic restrictions.
As a result, MBAG identified an expanded vehicle scope covering vehicles produced up to the implementation of a modified brake hose design in series production.
MBAG subsequently identified the potentially affected vehicles in the field.
On September 25, 2026, MBAG determined that a potential safety risk cannot be ruled out for the expanded vehicle population and decided to expand the recall.
This recall expands upon the vehicle population subject to Recall No. 25V116, filed on February 24, 2025.
The Field Engineering Activity was formally launched in March 2026.
